headline: Obaidul Quader and 6 others face ICT verdict today in humanity crimes case
summary: The International Crimes Tribunal-2 will deliver its judgment on atrocities committed during the 2024 July Uprising, with all seven accused currently absconding.
details: The International Crimes Tribunal-2 is set to deliver its verdict today in a crimes against humanity case involving former AL general secretary Obaidul Quader and six others.
The prosecution alleges that Quader used his command over law enforcement and party cadres to violently suppress the quota reform movement starting July 1, 2024.
The case involves allegations of widespread, systematic attacks on civilians, resulting in over 1,400 deaths and 25,000 serious injuries, according to the prosecution.
Other accused include former state minister Mohammad Ali Arafat, AL Joint General Secretary AFM Bahauddin Nasim, and Jubo League leaders Sheikh Fazle Shams Parash and Moinul Hossain Nikhil.
The charges also extend to Chhatra League leaders Saddam Hussain and Sheikh Wali Asif Enan for allegedly coordinating attacks and assembling armed cadres.
The trial, which began on February 17, followed an investigation that started on June 18, 2025, and concluded with closing arguments in August.
All seven accused are currently absconding and are not present for the verdict.
caption:
Over 1,400 killed and 25,000 injured. Today, Obaidul Quader and six others face the ICT verdict.

The International Crimes Tribunal-2 is set to deliver its verdict today in a crimes against humanity case involving former AL general secretary Obaidul Quader and six others.

The prosecution alleges that Quader used his command over law enforcement and party cadres to violently suppress the quota reform movement starting July 1, 2024.

The case involves allegations of widespread, systematic attacks on civilians, resulting in over 1,400 deaths and 25,000 serious injuries, according to the prosecution.

Other accused include former state minister Mohammad Ali Arafat, AL Joint General Secretary AFM Bahauddin Nasim, and Jubo League leaders Sheikh Fazle Shams Parash and Moinul Hossain Nikhil.

The charges also extend to Chhatra League leaders Saddam Hussain and Sheikh Wali Asif Enan for allegedly coordinating attacks and assembling armed cadres.

The trial, which began on February 17, followed an investigation that started on June 18, 2025, and concluded with closing arguments in August.

All seven accused are currently absconding and are not present for the verdict.

headline_marked: Bureaucrats [[use project vehicles for personal gain]] despite rules
headline: Bureaucrats use project vehicles for personal gain despite rules
summary: Officials from various ministries and the Anti-Corruption Commission are allegedly using LGED project cars for personal use, violating government regulations.
details: An investigation reveals that high-ranking bureaucrats are using SUVs and other vehicles from the Local Government Engineering Department (LGED) for personal use, despite rules stating project cars must only be used for project work.

The list of 261 vehicles includes 211 SUVs, 41 double-cabin pickups, and 9 cars. Of these, 59 vehicles have been handed over to various ministries and agencies, including the Prime Minister's Office and the Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC).

The Local Government Division has the highest number of project cars, with 34 vehicles. Other recipients include the Planning Commission (10), the International Crimes Tribunal (6), and the Prime Minister's Office (3).

Transparency International Bangladesh (TIB) has described this as a 'collusive irregularity,' suggesting that agencies like the ACC and Planning Commission may be providing protection to LGED in exchange for these vehicles.

When questioned, some officials claimed they were not the only ones doing it, while LGED's Chief Engineer stated that vehicles were provided based on work requirements, though he could not confirm if the ACC or Planning Commission had cars.
The rules clearly state that project vehicles must be returned to the transport pool after a project ends, but many officials continue to use them even if they are not eligible for government cars.
